passage1.text: The weakening of the human connection to nature might be good for economic growth but is bad for people.A tipping point was reached in 2020 when human-made materials—such as steel,concrete and plastic— were found to weigh more than all life on Earth.Continuing to grow concrete forests rather than real ones is shortsighted.Simply being in the nearest wood has such health benefits that the Woodland Trust successfully lobbied for it to be prescribed by doctors. Yet slipping from popular culture is the wonder and beauty of the natural world.For every three nature- related words in hit songs ofthe 1950s,researchers found,there was only slightly more than one 50 years later.It is not a moment too soon that teenagers will be able to take a natural history test,given that for decades children have been able to name more video game characters than wildlife species. Part ofremedying this social disease would be for parliament to pass a "right to grow"law,allowing anyone to turn underused public spaces into vegetable and fruit gardens.The idea is for people to get back in touch with the soil—while producing food sustainably. Vegetable planting has a respectable tradition.In April 1649,locals responded to high prices and food shortages by cultivating vegetables on common land in Southern England.The practice ofthrowing seed bombs to turn vacant plots of land green took off in 1970s New York,and has been revived(使复活)by green-thumbed ( 有 园 艺 才 能 的 )social media influencers who defy local US regulations in a war on ugly spots in cities. Apart from the urgent task ofproviding more healthy nutrients to those who increasingly can't afford them, publicly accessible fruit and vegetable gardens connect what we eat to where it comes from—the means of production,if you will.They can make unlovely spaces lovely,and marry use and beauty as well as help promote a sense of community.Plants are also,of course,our first defence against species loss and climate change.Such planting is a small step for humanity—in the right direction.

passage2.text: Engineering in the U.S.has long been a male-dominated profession.Fifty years ago,it looked like that might change. In 1970,the percentage of women majoring in engineering was less than 1%.In 1979,that number was 9% Many hoped women would continue to enter the field at the same rate.But that's not what happened.Today,only 21%of engineering majors are women,a number largely unchanged since 2000. I am a historian who,along with my colleagues,surveyed 251 women engineers who graduated from college in the 1970s.These pioneers reflected on the challenges they faced—and had advice for women entering the field today. One survey taker explained,"The greatest challenge for me was continuing to believe in myself,when all the messages I was getting were that I would never be taken seriously or promoted or given raises at the same rate as men,who were clearly less qualified and not as smart as I was." A chemical engineer who worked in manufacturing agreed,"You have to prove yourselfjust because you are female.And you have to work twice as hard!" A civil engineer said,"We are'women engineers.'People don't refer to a man as a ‘man engineer'-he's an engineer.We are constantly reminded that we don't truly belong."Another civil engineer stated,"On many levels,you're never quite one of the groups." Women also talked about family caregiving responsibilities.A retired vice president from a major chemical company stated,"Young women engineers are on an equal footing until they have children,then they struggle to balance work and family—and compete with men who don't have the same household responsibilities." But over the years things have changed a lot.Young women engineers are more accepted mostly because there arejust more ofthem. Many women engineers hailed the benefits of their chosen career.A program manager in manufacturing stated that engineering is the best degree.A mechanical engineer said,“It will give you the flexibility to do almost anything.It is also satisfying to see the effects ofwhat you have done."

paragraphs.A: Few topics have been so endlessly analysed as work-life balance.The quest to attain this mysterious state has dominated discussion around careers for years—especially for working parents.The concept is often presented as something to achieve,or a goal to reach.And once you've reached it,congratulations:you've made it;you're a successful human being of the 21st century.
paragraphs.B: But the problem is that we often tell ourselves:"I'm going to put in eight hours'worth of work,and then I'm going to put in eight hours'worth of 'me time',which will include my family,my hobbies,my workout,my everything,"says Anat Lechner,clinical associate professor of management at New York University."I don't think it's such a simple formula."
paragraphs.C: And,according to new findings,it may not be.Some researchers are now encouraging us to stop thinking about work-life balance as an achievement that you either hit or don't.Instead,they suggest it may be more of a lifelong process—a continuous,never-ending exercise that requires self-awareness and timely adjustments.Researchers Ioana Lupu and Mayra Ruiz-Castro argue that work-life balance is "a cycle,not an achievement".In their 2020 study,the researchers interviewed nearly 80 employees at two London-based firms—an equal number of men and women between the ages of 30 and 50,all with at least one dependent child—who worked in middle or senior management roles.
paragraphs.D: Although it sounds like the respondents had a lot in common,here's what separated them:about 30%of the men and 50%of the women reported resisting working long hours.The other respondents,meanwhile,all worked long hours because they thought that's what successful professionals should do.
paragraphs.E: Lupu and Ruiz-Castro looked at those who rejected the long hours and they found that those workers actually had strikingly similar strategies for maintaining their work-life balance.They had a tendency to reflect and question assumptions in the name of self-awareness and regularly took steps to adjust the things standing in their way to work-life balance.
paragraphs.F: Lupu and Ruiz-Castro identified five steps that the respondents in the study who had better work-life balance used in their jobs.First,they paused and reconsidered beliefs such as "I'm a professional,so I should work, work,work",and asked themselves questions like,"What's currently causing me stress?”Second,after identifying the cause,they zeroed in on their resultant emotions.Did they feel angry,sad,energised?Third, they reprioritised,asking"Is working long hours really worth cutting back on family time?",for example. Fourth,they considered their alternatives:is there anything at work that could be changed to accommodate these new priorities?And finally,they implemented changes,like asking their supervisor for greater flexibility,or deciding not to take on every project that comes their way.
paragraphs.G: This five-step process is something anyone can adopt.Going through the steps,and constantly checking in with yourself,can help you shift and adapt your professional life to something that will better harmonise with your personal one.“Awareness of your emotional state is essential in order to determine the changes you want to make in your work and in your life,"says Lupu.
paragraphs.H: New York University's Lechner agrees that finding that balance is an ongoing pursuit.It's not simply about dividing up the hours in your day between work,the gym,kids and chores.If the underlying emotional sources of stress are still there,then the time you actually spend at home may not be enjoyable.“We come home and even though physically we are there,mentally we still may be processing things that happened at work.We're not present,"she says.What we call"work-life balance"is actually just a substitute to having a sense of fulfillment and contentment. D Of course,finding that balance probably shouldn't be something you have to do by yourself.Research by Erin Kelly,professor of work and organisation studies at MIT,shows companies and managers can play a key role in creating a better environment for workers.For her book Overload:How Good Jobs Went Bad and What to Do about It,she and co-author Phyllis Moen split more than 1,000 employees at a Fortune 500 company into two groups,one that worked under a management redesign and one that continued working within the existing management structure. J)Under the management redesign,many steps were taken to ensure better work-life balance and prevent burnout(精疲力竭).Managers were regularly reminded to explicitly support their employees.Workers were allowed to make changes,like cancelling 9 am meetings.All of this was done in the name of increasing job satisfaction and giving workers greater flexibility,and to assure workers that it was something management was committed to.Unsurprisingly,Kelly and Moen found that employees in the redesign group reported less stress and less burnout.They were less likely to quit their jobs;indeed,over the next four years,they were 40%less likely to quit than those who kept working under the old policies. K)“Work-life balance is understood to be an individual's response,so people think ‘it's up to me to manage the craziness of my work life'",says Kelly.But organisations need to examine the demands they're placing on employees."The root problem is not how the two pieces of work and life come together.It's that we have unrealistic expectations of what we're asked to do on the work side."If your workplace isn't an environment where work-life balance is possible in the first place,any effort you attempt to make toward it on a personal level will be in vain. L)That's a conversation that appears to be gathering pace.The new prevalence of remote and flexible working models will likely all play important roles in how we balance our professional and personal lives.And if it seems like finding that perfect balance remains difficult to achieve,the experts say that keeping some perspective can help.For millions of people,work is about being able to put food on the table.Talking about work-life balance "is a very privileged conversation”,says Lechner."If we're reflecting,maybe we should also reflect on that."

A rare thundersnow event has taken place in Scotland. And alarmed locals contacted police, thinking they
had heard bombs going off. The phenomenon happens when thunder and lightning mix with a heavy snowstorm
[5] sometimes causing loud claps that can be confused with explosions.
One person described it as a loud boom, similar to a plane crash. Another person was woken up in the middle of
the night by what he thought was early construction work starting. The noise was powerful enough to shake buildings
and set off car alarms. The police were flooded with many calls from the public. [6] And they sent out a message
asking people to remain calm. The police assured everyone that it was just thunder and lightning rather than some
military exercise. The weather was the coldest it had been for the season, [7] so people were warned to be careful when
traveling outside. In particular, dangerous conditions such as icy roads or wet ground could cause difficulty for drivers.
The rail service also announced potential disruptions to trains due to the deep snow. Some roads were also closed
because of the severe weather.

questions.script:
Kids need time every day to run, jump, stretch and play.These experiences have been shown to build children's
confidence and pleasure in physical activities, develop their motor skills, and even improve emotional well-being
[16] To begin with, children seem to have a natural desire to overcome challenges and take risks. Taking healthy
risks through physical movement builds children's confidence and ability to solve problems and persist through
frustration. Secondly, movement activities build children's big body skills such as coordination and balance, as well as
the fine motor skills they need for tasks like writing, tying their shoes, or throwing and catching a ball. [17] Thirdly.
according to the American Psychological Association, regular physical activity (and especially outdoor activity) reduces
children's stress and depression, and improves their ability to focus and learn. Regular exercise can significantly
improve self-regulation and decrease disciplinary consequences for negative behavior. Physical activity provides a
positive outlet for frustration, anxiety, or anger and can become a healthy coping skill throughout life.[18] Finally,
we know that physical activity is important for our physical and mental health, and cultivating the habit of physical
activity starts early. Children are more likely to develop a lifelong love of physical activity from frequent positive early
experiences. Not every child enjoys competitive sports or playing with balls and that's OK. There are plenty of other
options such as imaginative play, non-competitive games, and gardening or nature experiences.

questions.script:
[19] A new study finds that job seekers are even willing to explore jobs with lower salaries when companies are
more diverse. It finds that sharing information about diversity makes job postings more attractive to job seekers, even
when pay is lower.
To conduct the study, the team partnered with an online job listings platform which emails postings relevant to
individuals and their job search criteria. For the course of the 11-week study, the platform emailed job listings to some
180,000 users placed in one of two conditions.[20] In the baseline condition, participants saw emails in the normal format,
with no information on diversity; in the diversity condition, participants saw a diversity score for each listing: information
about the race, gender, education, and language skills of a company's workforce compared to others in the same sector and
location. Information was then gathered on whether the email was opened, and which job listings were clicked on by each
user.
Participants in the diversity condition tended to click on job listings from companies with slightly higher diversity
scores than those in the baseline condition: [21] that is, participants seemed to be paying attention to information about
diversity, and using this when deciding whether to click on the listing. And the team also found that participants were
willing to look at listings with lower salaries if they came from companies with a higher diversity score.

as a source of attachment in the face of changing family structures.
Yet, very little research has focused on how dogs perceive and socially engage with children. [24] The great news
is that this study suggests dogs are paying a lot of attention to the kids that they live with," said Monique Udell, the

questions.stem: 第 26 空
questions.expl: (unique) 详解： 语法判断：空格前为“was not”，后为介词短语“in this regard”，需填入形容词作表语。 语义判断：上文提到莫里森39岁出版第一部小说、84岁出版最后一部，下文说“许多作家70多岁仍能创作出杰作”，说明莫里森的情况并非个例，“not unique”（并非独一无二）符合语境。 涉及知识点：形容词词义辨析（unique“独一无二的”），结合上下文逻辑（例证支撑观点，说明现象的普遍性）。

questions.expl: (literary) 详解： 语法判断：空格前为“such”，后为名词“accomplishments”，需填入形容词作定语。 语义判断：上文提到“许多作家创作出杰作”，“literary accomplishments”（文学成就）为固定搭配，符合“作家创作”的语境。 涉及知识点：形容词与名词的固定搭配（literary修饰accomplishments），结合话题场景（文学领域）。

questions.expl: 详解： 语法判断：空格前为“ability to produce and to”，后为名词“language”，需填入动词原形，与“produce”（产生、表达）并列。 语义判断：“produce and comprehend language”（表达和理解语言）符合“语言能力”的核心范畴，与上文“说话、写作、学习新词汇”呼应。 涉及知识点：动词词义辨析（comprehend“理解”），并列结构的语义搭配（produce与comprehend分别对应“输出”与“输入”能力）。

questions.expl: (journey) 详解： 语法判断：空格前为不定冠词“a”，后为that引导的定语从句，需填入名词。 语义判断：定语从句“从婴儿时期开始并持续一生”描述的是一个“过程、旅程”，“journey”（旅程）比喻语言学习的终身性，符合语境。 涉及知识点：名词词义辨析（journey“旅程”），比喻修辞的理解（将语言学习比作终身旅程）。

questions.stem: 第 31 空
questions.expl: (actually) 详解： 语法判断：空格所在句子主谓宾完整（our knowledge... improve），需填入副词作状语。 语义判断：下文举例说明60岁以上老人词汇量高于大学生，证明语言能力“实际上”在中老年会提升，“actually”（事实上）强调与普遍认知（年龄增长能力下降）相反的情况。 涉及知识点：副词词义辨析（actually“实际上”），转折逻辑的强化（突出研究发现与普遍认知的差异）。

questions.stem: 第 32 空
questions.expl: (sample) 详解： 语法判断：空格前为不定冠词“a”，后为介词短语“of college students”，需填入名词。 语义判断：研究中“研究一组大学生样本”符合实验逻辑，“a sample of”（……的样本）为固定搭配，与前文“adults over sixty”形成对比研究对象。 涉及知识点：名词词义辨析（sample“样本”），实验类文本的固定表达（study a sample of）。

questions.stem: 36. According to a management expert,work-life balance is not as simple as giving equal amounts of time to work and personal life.
questions.expl: 题干关键词“a management expert”“not as simple as”“equal amounts of time”对应B段。纽约大学管理学教授阿纳特·莱希纳指出，人们误以为“8小时工作+8小时个人时间”就是工作生活平衡，但这并非简单公式。题干是对该观点的概括，其中“equal amounts of time”对应原文“eight hours' worth of work + eight hours' worth of 'me time'”。 涉及知识点：关键词定位（人名+核心观点），同义转述（not as simple as = don't think it's such a simple formula）。

questions.stem: 37. Research found that those who are given greater flexibility at work are less stressed and more likely to stay in theirjobs.
questions.expl: 题干关键词“greater flexibility”“less stressed”“more likely to stay”对应J段。研究发现，管理结构重新设计后（允许员工灵活调整工作，如取消早会），员工压力更小、离职率更低（比旧政策组低40%）。题干是对该研究结果的同义转述，其中“more likely to stay in their jobs”对应“less likely to quit their jobs”。 涉及知识点：实验类文本定位（两组对比），同义替换（greater flexibility = giving workers greater flexibility；less stressed = reported less stress）。

questions.stem: 38. Workers who rejected working long hours tended to make regular adjustments in order to achieve work-life balance.
questions.expl: 题干关键词“rejected working long hours”“make regular adjustments”对应E段。研究发现，拒绝长时间工作的员工会通过“反思假设、定期调整阻碍因素”来维持工作生活平衡。题干中“make regular adjustments in order to achieve work-life balance”直接对应原文“regularly took steps to adjust the things standing in their way to work-life balance”。 涉及知识点：细节定位（核心动作+目的），概括总结（将原文的具体策略提炼为“make regular adjustments”）。

questions.stem: 39. Talking about work-life balance is said to be a privilege reserved for the better-off,not for those who barely make a living.
questions.expl: 题干关键词“Talking about work-life balance”“a privilege”“barely make a living”对应L段。莱希纳指出，对数百万人而言，工作只是为了养家糊口，谈论工作生活平衡是“富有特权的对话”。题干中“a privilege reserved for the better-off”对应原文“a very privileged conversation”，“barely make a living”对应“put food on the table”。 涉及知识点：观点类文本定位（人物+核心评价），同义转述（privilege的语境理解）。

questions.stem: 40. Knowing one's emotional state is of utmost importance in deciding what changes to make for a better work- life balance.
questions.expl: 题干关键词“emotional state”“utmost importance”“deciding what changes”对应G段。卢普强调，“意识到自己的情绪状态对于决定工作和生活中的改变至关重要”。题干中“Knowing one's emotional state is of utmost importance”对应原文“Awareness of your emotional state is essential”，“deciding what changes to make”对应“determine the changes you want to make”。 涉及知识点：人物观点定位（直接引语），同义替换（utmost importance = essential）。

questions.stem: 41. More female professionals reported being reluctant to work overtime than their male counter
questions.expl: 题干关键词“More female professionals”“reluctant to work overtime”“male counterparts”对应D段。研究显示，30%的男性和50%的女性抵制长时间工作，即更多女性不愿加班。题干中“More female professionals reported... than their male counterparts”对应原文“30% of the men and 50% of the women reported”，“reluctant to work overtime”对应“resisting working long hours”。 涉及知识点：数据对比定位（男女比例差异），同义替换（reluctant to work overtime = resisting working long hours）。

questions.stem: 42. Without organisational support,any personal effort to maintain work-life balance will be unsuccessful.
questions.expl: 题干关键词“Without organisational support”“personal effort”“unsuccessful”对应K段。凯利指出，若工作场所本身不具备平衡工作生活的环境，个人努力将徒劳。题干中“Without organisational support”对应原文“If your workplace isn't an environment where work-life balance is possible”，“unsuccessful”对应“will be in vain”。 涉及知识点：条件关系定位（if引导的否定条件），同义替换（organisational support = workplace environment；unsuccessful = in vain）。

questions.stem: 43. The question of how to achieve work-life balance has long been the main subject of discussion among workers.
questions.expl: 题干关键词“The question of how to achieve work-life balance”“main subject of discussion”对应A段。原文提到“工作生活平衡是被无休止分析的话题，对其的追求主导了职业相关讨论”。题干中“has long been the main subject of discussion”对应原文“has dominated discussion around careers for years”，“The question of how to achieve work-life balance”对应“The quest to attain this mysterious state”。 涉及知识点：主旨句定位（段落开头核心话题），同义替换（quest = question；attain = achieve）。

questions.stem: 44. You may not actually experience emotional wellbeing at home ifyou remain occupied with what happened at work.
questions.expl: 题干关键词“not actually experience emotional wellbeing at home”“remain occupied with what happened at work”对应H段。原文提到，若工作中的压力情绪未消除，即使在家，精神仍在处理工作事务，导致居家时间不愉快。题干中“not actually experience emotional wellbeing”对应“the time you actually spend at home may not be enjoyable”，“remain occupied with what happened at work”对应“mentally we still may be processing things that happened at work”。 涉及知识点：因果关系定位（压力来源→居家体验），概括总结（将原文的心理状态描述提炼为题干的条件句）。

questions.stem: 45. Some researchers suggest that work-life balance is not a goal to achieve,but a process for life to be adjusted promptly.
questions.expl: 题干关键词“Some researchers”“not a goal to achieve”“a process for life to be adjusted promptly”对应C段。研究人员指出，不应将工作生活平衡视为“达成或未达成的成就”，而应是“需要及时调整的终身过程”。题干中“not a goal to achieve”对应“stop thinking about work-life balance as an achievement”，“a process for life to be adjusted promptly”对应“a lifelong process... timely adjustments”。 涉及知识点：研究观点定位（researchers' argument），同义替换（goal = achievement；promptly adjusted = timely adjustments）。

questions.stem: 46. What does the author want to emphasise in the first paragraph?

options.A: The year 2020 was a big turning point in human history.
options.B: Economic growth benefits people little in the long run.
options.C: It is unwise to weaken the human connection to nature.
options.D: It is harmful to mankind to use human-made materials.

questions.expl: 题干定位到第一段。第一段核心观点为“人类与自然联系的弱化对经济增长有益，但对人类不利”，并以2020年人造材料重量超过地球生物重量为例，强调“种植混凝土森林（城市化）而非真正森林是短视行为”。C项“削弱人与自然的联系是不明智的”是对该段主旨的概括，正确。 干扰项分析：A项“2020年是重大转折点”是例证中的细节，非核心观点；B项“经济增长对人几乎无益”与原文“可能有利于经济增长”矛盾；D项“使用人造材料有害”过度解读，原文批判的是“过度依赖人造材料导致与自然脱节”，而非人造材料本身。 涉及知识点：段落主旨提炼，区分“核心观点”与“例证细节”，把握转折逻辑（but连接的利弊对比）。

questions.stem: 47. What did researchers find about popular culture?

options.A: It is increasingly detached from the natural world.
options.B: It is filled with all kinds ofvideo game characters.
options.C: It is especially appealing to the taste ofteenagers.
options.D: It is stillimpacted by the hit songs of the 1950s.

questions.expl: 题干定位到第二段，关键词“popular culture”。第二段首句点明“自然界的神奇与美丽在大众文化中逐渐消失”，随后通过两个例证支撑：①20世纪50年代热门歌曲中自然相关词汇是50年后的3倍；②孩子能说出更多电子游戏角色而非野生动物名称。A项“越来越脱离自然界”是对该段主旨的概括，正确。 干扰项分析：B项“充斥着电子游戏角色”过度推断，原文仅说孩子对游戏角色更熟悉，未说大众文化“充斥”此类内容；C项“迎合青少年口味”未被提及；D项“受50年代热门歌曲影响”与原文“50年代与自然相关词汇更多”矛盾。 涉及知识点：例证支持主旨的逻辑分析，通过具体案例提炼段落核心趋势。

questions.stem: 48. What does the author propose people do?

options.A: Take measures to ensure sustainable food development.
options.B: Reconnect with nature through the right to grow.
options.C: Stand by the parliament in fighting social diseases.
options.D: Cover public spaces with fruit trees and vegetable plants.

questions.expl: 题干定位到第三段，关键词“author propose people do”。第三段提出解决方案：议会通过“种植权”法律，允许将未充分利用的公共空间改为蔬果园，目的是“让人们重新与土地建立联系，同时可持续生产食物”。B项“通过种植权重新与大自然建立联系”是对该提议核心目的的概括，正确。 干扰项分析：A项“确保粮食可持续发展”是提议的附加效果，非核心目的；C项“与社会弊病作斗争”扩大范围，原文仅说该法律是“治疗社会弊病的部分措施”；D项“在公共场所种植果蔬”是提议的具体行为，而非作者希望人们达成的核心目标（核心是“重新连接自然”）。 涉及知识点：细节理解（提议的“目的”与“行为”区分），概括总结（提炼提议的核心意图而非表面行为）。

questions.stem: 49. What do we learn from the passage about vegetable planting?

options.A: It all started in 1649 in Southern England.
options.B: It is protected by US government regulations. 7 ·2024年12月四级真题(第一套) ·
options.C: It has long been used to increase food supply and improve urban landscape.
options.D: It has been popularised worldwide with the increasing influence of social media.

questions.expl: 题干定位到第四段，关键词“vegetable planting”。第四段列举两个案例：①1649年英格兰南部居民种植蔬菜应对粮食短缺；②20世纪70年代纽约用“种子炸弹”绿化空地，现被社交媒体影响者复兴。由此可概括“蔬菜种植长期用于增加食物供应和改善城市景观”，C项正确。 干扰项分析：A项“始于1649年英格兰南部”错误，原文仅说该年有相关实践，未表明“起源”；B项“受美国政府法规保护”与原文“社交媒体影响者违抗美国当地法规”矛盾；D项“全球普及”过度推断，原文仅提及英格兰、纽约的案例，未涉及“全球范围”。 涉及知识点：例证归纳，通过多个不同时期、地区的案例提炼共性功能（增加食物供应+改善景观）。

questions.stem: 50. What can publicly accessible fruit and vegetable gardens do apart from their practical functions?

options.A: Raise people's environmental awareness.
options.B: Add to the great variety ofplant species.
options.C: Act as the first defence against natural disasters.
options.D: Enhance people's community spirit.

questions.expl: 题干定位到最后一段，关键词“publicly accessible fruit and vegetable gardens”“apart from their practical functions”。最后一段提到，除了提供健康营养品的实用功能外，公众蔬果园还能“让丑陋空间变可爱，结合实用与美观，帮助增强社区意识”。D项“增强人们的社区精神”对应“promote a sense of community”，正确。 干扰项分析：A项“提高环保意识”、B项“增加植物种类多样性”均未被提及；C项“抵御自然灾害的第一道防线”错误，原文说“植物是抵御物种损失和气候变化的第一道防线”，而非蔬果园本身。 涉及知识点：细节定位（区分“实用功能”与“附加价值”），同义替换（community spirit = sense of community）。

questions.stem: 51. What does the passage say about the engineering profession in the United States?

options.A: It has seen a change in attitude towards women engineers since 1979.
options.B: It witnessed a significant increase in women engineers in the 1970s
options.C: It has experienced the gradual weakening ofmale dominance.
options.D: It boasted the largest number of engineering majors in 2000.

questions.expl: 题干定位到前两段，关键词“engineering profession in the United States”。第二段数据显示：1970年女性工程专业学生比例不足1%，1979年升至9%，说明20世纪70年代女性工程师数量显著增加，B项正确。 干扰项分析：A项“1979年后态度改变”与原文“1979年后比例停滞不前”矛盾；C项“男性主导地位逐渐削弱”错误，原文说“2000年后女性比例基本不变，仍仅21%”，男性主导地位未削弱；D项“2000年工程专业学生最多”未被提及，原文仅说2000年后女性比例不变。 涉及知识点：数据解读（比例变化→数量趋势），时间节点区分（1970s vs 1979 vs 2000）。

questions.stem: 52. What does one survey taker say was her greatest challenge?

options.A: Not to feel superior to less qualified male engineers.
options.B: Not to take seriously all the messages she was getting.
options.C: Not to think highly ofher qualifications when promoted or given a pay raise.
options.D: Not to lose self-confidence though constantly discouraged or unfairly treated.

questions.expl: 题干定位到第四段，关键词“one survey taker”“greatest challenge”。受访者表示，最大的挑战是“当所有信息都表明自己受重视、晋升、加薪的速度赶不上资质不如自己的男性时，仍要相信自己”，即“即使遭遇不公平对待和挫折，也不失去自信”，D项正确。 干扰项分析：A项“不觉得比男性优越”与原文“男性不如自己有资格”矛盾；B项“不认真对待收到的信息”未被提及，受访者的挑战是“面对负面信息仍保持自信”，而非忽视信息；C项“晋升加薪时不自视甚高”与原文无关。 涉及知识点：直接引语理解，提炼人物面临的核心矛盾（外部不公平对待→内部自我信念坚守）。

questions.stem: 53. How do women engineers frequently feel according to the two civil engineers?

options.A: Disqualified on many levels.
options.B: Excluded from the group.
options.C: Overworked by their organizations.
options.D: Looked down upon by male colleagues.

questions.expl: 题干定位到第六段，关键词“two civil engineers”。第一位土木工程师提到“人们称呼我们为‘女工程师’，而男性仅被称为‘工程师’，我们常被提醒不属于这个群体”；第二位表示“在很多层面上，永远不是群体中的一员”。核心感受是“被排斥”，B项正确。 干扰项分析：A项“在很多层面不合格”错误，原文说“男性不如自己有资格”，说明女性具备资质；C项“工作过多”、D项“被男同事瞧不起”均未被提及，原文强调的是“身份上的排斥”而非“工作强度”或“态度歧视”。 涉及知识点：人物观点归纳，通过两位受访者的共同表述提炼核心感受（被群体排除）。

questions.stem: 54. What probably makes young women engineers more accepted nowadays?

options.A: Their success in gaining an equal footing.
options.B: Their ability to balance work and family.
options.C: The change in their responsibilities.
options.D: The increase in their number.

questions.expl: 题干定位到倒数第二段，关键词“more accepted nowadays”。原文明确指出“年轻女工程师更易被接受，主要是因为她们的人数增多了”，D项正确。 干扰项分析：A项“获得平等地位”与原文“有孩子后难以平衡工作家庭，需与无家庭责任的男性竞争”矛盾；B项“平衡工作家庭的能力”是女性面临的挑战，非被接受的原因；C项“责任变化”未被提及。 涉及知识点：因果关系定位（原文直接给出“原因=人数增加”），避免过度解读其他无关因素。

questions.stem: 55. What can we conclude about many female engineers from the statement ofa mechanical engineer?

options.A: They take great pride in their chosen career.
options.B: They have reaped the benefits ofbeing flexible.
options.C: They enjoy doing engineering to the best degree.
options.D: They have proved capable of doing almost anything.

questions.expl: 题干定位到最后一段，关键词“a mechanical engineer”。最后一段首句提到“许多女工程师为自己选择的职业所带来的好处欢呼雀跃”，机械工程师补充“工程学能让人灵活做几乎任何事，看到工作成效令人满足”。由此可推断，女工程师对自己的职业感到自豪，A项正确。 干扰项分析：B项“从灵活性中获益”是机械工程师的直接陈述，无需推断，题干要求“conclude”（推断），故排除；C项“喜欢把工程做到最好”未被提及，原文强调的是职业带来的满足感而非“极致追求”；D项“证明自己几乎无所不能”过度解读，原文说“灵活做几乎任何事”，而非“有能力做任何事”。 涉及知识点：推理判断（结合段落主旨与具体陈述推断隐含态度），区分“直接陈述”与“隐含结论”。
